mn75:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living among the Kurus, at a town of the Kurus called Kammāsadhamma, on a spread of grass in the fire-hall of a brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan.
mn75:2.1: Then when it was morning, the Blessed One dressed, and taking his bowl and outer robe, he went into Kammāsadhamma for alms.
mn75:2.2: When he had wandered for alms in Kammāsadhamma and had returned from his alms round, after the meal he went to a certain grove for the day’s abiding.
mn75:2.3: Having plunged into that grove, he sat down at the root of a tree for the day’s abiding.
mn75:3.1: Then Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer, walking and wandering for exercise, went to the fire-hall of the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan.
mn75:3.2: Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer saw a spread of grass made ready in the fire-hall of the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan.
mn75:3.3: Seeing it, he said to the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan:
mn75:3.4: “Whose is this spread of grass made ready in Master Bhāradvāja’s fire-hall? It looks like a resting place for an ascetic.”
mn75:4.1: “There is, Master Māgaṇḍiya, the ascetic Gotama, a son of the Sakyans, who has gone forth from a Sakyan clan.
mn75:4.2: Now a good report of that Master Gotama has been spread about thus:
mn75:4.3: ‘That Blessed One is such since he is an Arahant, fully enlightened, accomplished in true knowledge and conduct, sublime, knower of the world, unsurpassed leader of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, enlightened, blessed.’
mn75:4.4: This is the resting place made ready for that Master Gotama.”
mn75:5.1: “It is indeed an ill sight, Master Bhāradvāja, that we see;
mn75:5.2: it is indeed an ill sight, Master Bhāradvāja, that we see,
mn75:5.3: in that we see the resting place of that Master Gotama, the wreaker of being.”[^1]
mn75:5.5: guard that speech of yours, Māgaṇḍiya.
mn75:5.6: For many wise nobles, wise brahmins, wise householders, and wise ascetics have full confidence in that Master Gotama, and are trained in the noble method, the wholesome Dhamma.”
mn75:5.7: “Even if we were to see that Master Gotama face to face, Master Bhāradvāja, we would say to his face:
mn75:5.8: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a wreaker of being.’
mn75:5.10: Because that is how it comes down to us in our scriptures.”
mn75:5.11: “If Master Māgaṇḍiya does not mind, I will report that to the ascetic Gotama.”
mn75:5.12: “Let Master Bhāradvāja not trouble himself; say to him just what has been said.”
mn75:6.1: The Blessed One heard, with the divine ear element, purified and surpassing the human, this conversation between the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan and Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer.
mn75:6.2: Then when it was evening, the Blessed One rose from meditation and went to the fire-hall of the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, and sat down on the spread of grass made ready.
mn75:6.3: Then the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan went to the Blessed One and exchanged greetings with him.
mn75:6.4: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. The Blessed One then said to the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, as he sat at one side:
mn75:6.5: “Bhāradvāja, did you have some conversation with Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer concerning this very spread of grass?”
mn75:6.6: When this was said, the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, alarmed and with hair standing on end, said to the Blessed One:
mn75:6.7: “It was just this that we wanted to report to Master Gotama,
mn75:6.8: but Master Gotama has told it though it was not told to him.”
mn75:7.1: Now this conversation between the Blessed One and the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan was left unfinished,
mn75:7.2: for then Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer, walking and wandering for exercise, went to the Blessed One at the fire-hall of the brahmin of the Bhāradvāja clan, and exchanged greetings with him.
mn75:7.3: When the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he sat down at one side. The Blessed One then said to Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer, as he sat at one side:
mn75:8.1: “Māgaṇḍiya, the eye delights in forms, takes delight in forms, rejoices in forms.
mn75:8.2: That is tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained in the Tathāgata, and he teaches the Dhamma for its restraint.
mn75:8.3: Was it with reference to this, Māgaṇḍiya, that you said:
mn75:8.4: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a wreaker of being’?”
mn75:8.5: “It was with reference to this, Master Gotama, that I said:
mn75:8.6: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a wreaker of being.’
mn75:8.8: Because that is how it comes down to us in our scriptures.”
mn75:8.11: the tongue delights in flavours, takes delight in flavours, rejoices in flavours.
mn75:8.12: That is tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained in the Tathāgata, and he teaches the Dhamma for its restraint.
mn75:8.13: Was it with reference to this, Māgaṇḍiya, that you said:
mn75:8.14: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a wreaker of being’?”
mn75:8.15: “It was with reference to this, Master Gotama, that I said:
mn75:8.16: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a wreaker of being.’
mn75:8.18: Because that is how it comes down to us in our scriptures.”
mn75:8.19: “The body, Māgaṇḍiya, delights in tangibles, takes delight in tangibles …
mn75:8.20: the mind delights in mental objects, takes delight in mental objects, rejoices in mental objects.
mn75:8.21: That is tamed, guarded, protected, and restrained in the Tathāgata, and he teaches the Dhamma for its restraint.
mn75:8.22: Was it with reference to this, Māgaṇḍiya, that you said:
mn75:8.23: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a wreaker of being’?”
mn75:8.24: “It was with reference to this, Master Gotama, that I said:
mn75:8.25: ‘The ascetic Gotama is a wreaker of being.’
mn75:8.27: Because that is how it comes down to us in our scriptures.”
mn75:9.2: suppose someone had formerly amused himself with forms cognizable by the eye that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust; and on a later occasion, having known as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of forms, he abandoned craving for forms, removed the fever for forms, and dwelt without thirst, his mind stilled within.
mn75:9.3: What would you have to say about him, Māgaṇḍiya?”
mn75:9.6: suppose someone had formerly amused himself with sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn75:9.7: with odours cognizable by the nose …
mn75:9.8: with flavours cognizable by the tongue …
mn75:9.9: with tangibles cognizable by the body that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust,
mn75:9.10: and on a later occasion, having known as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of tangibles, he abandoned craving for tangibles, removed the fever for tangibles, and dwelt without thirst, his mind stilled within.
mn75:9.11: What would you have to say about him, Māgaṇḍiya?”
mn75:10.1: “As for me, Māgaṇḍiya, formerly, when I lived the home life, I was furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual desire, and I amused myself with forms cognizable by the eye that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust; with sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn75:10.2: with odours cognizable by the nose …
mn75:10.3: with flavours cognizable by the tongue …
mn75:10.4: with tangibles cognizable by the body that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust.
mn75:10.6: one for the rainy season, one for winter, and one for summer.
mn75:10.7: I lived in the rains palace for the four months of the rainy season, being entertained by musicians with no men among them, and I did not go down from that palace.
mn75:10.8: On a later occasion, having known as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of sensual pleasures, I abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, removed the fever for sensual pleasures, and I dwell without thirst, my mind stilled within.
mn75:10.9: I see other beings who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures, devoured by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with fever for sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures.
mn75:10.10: I do not envy them, nor do I delight in that.
mn75:10.12: Because, Māgaṇḍiya, there is a delight apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome things,
mn75:10.14: delighting in that delight, I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight in that.
mn75:11.1: Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, a householder or a householder’s son, rich, with great wealth and great possessions, furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual desire, were to amuse himself with forms cognizable by the eye …
mn75:11.3: with tangibles that are wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust.
mn75:11.4: Having conducted himself well in body, speech, and mind, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he might be reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, in the company of the gods of the Thirty-three.
mn75:11.5: There, in the Nandana Grove, surrounded by a throng of nymphs, furnished and endowed with the five cords of heavenly sensual desire, he might amuse himself.
mn75:11.6: He might see a householder or a householder’s son furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual desire, amusing himself.
mn75:11.7: What do you think, Māgaṇḍiya, would that son of the gods, in the Nandana Grove, surrounded by a throng of nymphs, furnished and endowed with the five cords of heavenly sensual desire, and amusing himself, envy that householder or householder’s son, or would he be drawn back to human sensual pleasures, to the five cords of human sensual desire?”
mn75:11.10: Because, Master Gotama, heavenly sensual pleasures are more excellent and sublime than human sensual pleasures.”
mn75:12.1: “So too, Māgaṇḍiya, formerly, when I lived the home life, I was furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual desire, and I amused myself with forms cognizable by the eye that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust; with sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn75:12.2: with odours cognizable by the nose …
mn75:12.3: with flavours cognizable by the tongue …
mn75:12.4: with tangibles cognizable by the body that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust.
mn75:12.5: On a later occasion, having known as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of sensual pleasures, I abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, removed the fever for sensual pleasures, and I dwell without thirst, my mind stilled within.
mn75:12.6: I see other beings who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures, devoured by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with fever for sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures; I do not envy them, nor do I delight in that.
mn75:12.8: Because, Māgaṇḍiya, there is a delight apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome things,
mn75:12.10: delighting in that delight, I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight in that.
mn75:13.1: Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, a leper with sores and blisters on his limbs, being devoured by worms, scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails, were to cauterize his body over a pit of burning coals.
mn75:13.2: His friends and companions, his relatives and kin, would bring him a surgeon to treat him.
mn75:13.3: The surgeon would make medicine for him.
mn75:13.4: Through that medicine, he might be freed from the leprosy, and might be healthy and happy, independent, his own master, able to go where he likes.
mn75:13.5: He might see another leper with sores and blisters on his limbs, being devoured by worms, scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails, cauterizing his body over a pit of burning coals.
mn75:13.7: would that man envy that leper his pit of burning coals or his use of medicine?”
mn75:13.10: Because, Master Gotama, when there is illness, there is need for medicine, and when there is no illness, there is no need for medicine.”
mn75:14.1: “So too, Māgaṇḍiya, formerly, when I lived the home life, I was furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual desire, and I amused myself with forms cognizable by the eye that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust; with sounds cognizable by the ear …
mn75:14.2: with odours cognizable by the nose …
mn75:14.3: with flavours cognizable by the tongue …
mn75:14.4: with tangibles cognizable by the body that were wished for, desired, agreeable, likeable, connected with sensual desire, and provocative of lust.
mn75:14.5: On a later occasion, having known as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of sensual pleasures, I abandoned craving for sensual pleasures, removed the fever for sensual pleasures, and I dwell without thirst, my mind stilled within.
mn75:14.6: I see other beings who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures, devoured by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with fever for sensual pleasures, indulging in sensual pleasures.
mn75:14.7: I do not envy them, nor do I delight in that.
mn75:14.9: Because, Māgaṇḍiya, there is a delight apart from sensual pleasures, apart from unwholesome things,
mn75:14.11: delighting in that delight, I do not envy what is inferior, nor do I delight in that.
mn75:15.1: Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, a leper with sores and blisters on his limbs, being devoured by worms, scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails, were to cauterize his body over a pit of burning coals.
mn75:15.2: His friends and companions, his relatives and kin, would bring him a surgeon to treat him.
mn75:15.3: The surgeon would make medicine for him.
mn75:15.4: Through that medicine, he might be freed from the leprosy, and might be healthy and happy, independent, his own master, able to go where he likes.
mn75:15.5: Then two strong men, seizing him by both arms, might drag him towards a pit of burning coals.
mn75:15.7: would that man twist his body this way and that?”
mn75:15.10: Because, Master Gotama, that fire is painful to touch, causes great heat and great fever.”
mn75:15.12: is that fire painful to touch, causing great heat and great fever, only now, or was that fire also painful to touch, causing great heat and great fever, formerly?”
mn75:15.13: “That fire, Master Gotama, is painful to touch, causing great heat and great fever, both now and formerly.
mn75:15.14: But that leper, Master Gotama, with sores and blisters on his limbs, being devoured by worms, scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails, had his faculties impaired, and so acquired a mistaken perception of pleasure regarding that fire which was actually painful to touch.”
mn75:16.1: “So too, Māgaṇḍiya, sensual pleasures were painful to touch, causing great heat and great fever, in the past; sensual pleasures will be painful to touch, causing great heat and great fever, in the future; and sensual pleasures are painful to touch, causing great heat and great fever, now in the present.
mn75:16.2: But these beings, Māgaṇḍiya, who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures,[^3] who are devoured by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with fever for sensual pleasures, have their faculties impaired, and so acquire a mistaken perception of pleasure regarding sensual pleasures that are actually painful to touch.
mn75:17.1: Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, a leper with sores and blisters on his limbs, being devoured by worms, scratching the scabs off the openings of his wounds with his nails, cauterizes his body over a pit of burning coals.
mn75:17.2: The more that leper cauterizes his body over the pit of burning coals, the fouler, the more foul-smelling, and the more infected the openings of his wounds become; yet he finds a certain measure of satisfaction and enjoyment in scratching the openings of his wounds.
mn75:17.3: So too, Māgaṇḍiya, beings who are not free from lust for sensual pleasures, who are devoured by craving for sensual pleasures, burning with fever for sensual pleasures, indulge in sensual pleasures.
mn75:17.4: The more such beings indulge in sensual pleasures, the more their craving for sensual pleasures grows, and the more they burn with fever for sensual pleasures; yet they find a certain measure of satisfaction and enjoyment dependent on the five cords of sensual desire.
mn75:18.2: have you seen or heard of a king or a king’s minister, furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual desire, amusing himself, who dwelt or dwells or will dwell without thirst, his mind stilled within, without having abandoned craving for sensual pleasures and without having removed the fever for sensual pleasures?”
mn75:18.5: I too, Māgaṇḍiya, have neither seen nor heard of a king or a king’s minister, furnished and endowed with the five cords of sensual desire, amusing himself, who dwelt or dwells or will dwell without thirst, his mind stilled within, without having abandoned craving for sensual pleasures and without having removed the fever for sensual pleasures.
mn75:18.6: Rather, Māgaṇḍiya, any ascetics or brahmins who dwelt or dwell or will dwell without thirst, their minds stilled within, have all done so only after knowing as it actually is the origin, the disappearance, the gratification, the danger, and the escape in the case of sensual pleasures, and after abandoning craving for sensual pleasures and removing the fever for sensual pleasures.”
mn75:19.1: Then, on that occasion, the Blessed One uttered this exclamation:
mn75:19.4: and the Eightfold is the best of paths,
mn75:19.6: When this was said, Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:
mn75:19.7: “It is wonderful, Master Gotama, it is marvellous, Master Gotama.
mn75:19.8: How well this has been said by Master Gotama:
mn75:19.9: ‘Health is the highest gain, Nibbāna is the highest bliss.’
mn75:19.10: I too have heard this said by former teachers and their teachers among the wanderers:
mn75:19.11: ‘Health is the highest gain, Nibbāna is the highest bliss’;
mn75:19.12: this agrees with that, Master Gotama.”
mn75:19.13: “But, Māgaṇḍiya, as to what you have heard said by former teachers and their teachers among the wanderers:
mn75:19.14: ‘Health is the highest gain, Nibbāna is the highest bliss’—what is that health, and what is that Nibbāna?”
mn75:19.15: When this was said, Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer stroked his own limbs with his hand, saying:
mn75:19.16: “This, Master Gotama, is that health, this is that Nibbāna.
mn75:19.17: For I, Master Gotama, am now healthy and happy, and nothing afflicts me.”
mn75:20.1: “Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, there were a man blind from birth;
mn75:20.2: he could not see dark and light forms, could not see blue forms, could not see yellow forms, could not see red forms, could not see crimson forms, could not see what is even and uneven, could not see the stars, could not see the moon and sun.
mn75:20.3: He might hear a man with good eyesight saying:
mn75:20.4: ‘Good sirs, how fine is a white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean!’
mn75:20.5: He might go in search of a white cloth.
mn75:20.6: Then a certain man might deceive him with a grimy, oil-stained garment, saying:[^4]
mn75:20.7: ‘Good man, here is a white cloth for you, beautiful, spotless, and clean.’
mn75:20.8: He might accept it, and having accepted it, put it on, and having put it on, being pleased, utter words of pleasure:
mn75:20.9: ‘How fine is this white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean!’
mn75:20.11: would that man blind from birth have accepted that grimy, oil-stained garment, and put it on, and being pleased, uttered words of pleasure:
mn75:20.12: ‘How fine is this white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean!’ knowing and seeing, or out of faith in the man with good eyesight?”
mn75:20.13: “Not knowing and not seeing, Master Gotama, that man blind from birth would have accepted that grimy, oil-stained garment, and put it on, and being pleased, uttered words of pleasure:
mn75:20.14: ‘How fine is this white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean!’—out of faith in the man with good eyesight.”
mn75:21.1: “So too, Māgaṇḍiya, wanderers of other sects are blind, without eyes, not knowing health, not seeing Nibbāna, and yet they speak this verse:
mn75:21.2: ‘Health is the highest gain, Nibbāna is the highest bliss.’
mn75:21.3: This verse, Māgaṇḍiya, was spoken by former Arahants, the Fully Enlightened Ones:
mn75:21.6: and the Eightfold is the best of paths,
mn75:21.8: That verse has now gradually become a verse of ordinary people.
mn75:21.9: Now this body, Māgaṇḍiya, is a disease, a boil, a dart, a misery, an affliction; yet of this body, which is a disease, a boil, a dart, a misery, an affliction, you say:
mn75:21.10: ‘This, Master Gotama, is that health, this is that Nibbāna.’
mn75:21.11: For you, Māgaṇḍiya, have no noble eye by which you might know health and see Nibbāna.”
mn75:22.1: “I have such confidence in Master Gotama
mn75:22.2: that Master Gotama is able to teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might come to know health and see Nibbāna.”
mn75:22.3: “Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, there were a man blind from birth;
mn75:22.4: he could not see dark and light forms, could not see blue forms, could not see yellow forms, could not see red forms, could not see crimson forms, could not see what is even and uneven, could not see the stars, could not see the moon and sun.
mn75:22.5: His friends and companions, his relatives and kin, might bring him a surgeon to treat him.
mn75:22.6: The surgeon might make medicine for him.
mn75:22.7: But through that medicine his eyesight might not arise, and might not be purified.
mn75:22.9: would not that doctor reap nothing but weariness and vexation?”
mn75:22.11: “So too, Māgaṇḍiya, were I to teach you the Dhamma thus:
mn75:22.12: ‘This is health, this is Nibbāna,’ you would not know health, you would not see Nibbāna.
mn75:22.13: That would be nothing but weariness and vexation for me.”
mn75:23.1: “I have such confidence in Master Gotama
mn75:23.2: that Master Gotama is able to teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might come to know health and see Nibbāna.”
mn75:23.3: “Suppose, Māgaṇḍiya, there were a man blind from birth;
mn75:23.4: he could not see dark and light forms, could not see blue forms, could not see yellow forms, could not see red forms, could not see crimson forms, could not see what is even and uneven, could not see the stars, could not see the moon and sun.
mn75:23.5: He might hear a man with good eyesight saying:
mn75:23.6: ‘Good sirs, how fine is a white cloth, beautiful, spotless, and clean!’
mn75:23.7: He might go in search of a white cloth.
mn75:23.8: Then a certain man might deceive him with a grimy, oil-stained garment, saying:
mn75:23.9: ‘Good man, here is a white cloth for you, beautiful, spotless, and clean.’
mn75:23.10: He might accept it, and having accepted it, put it on.
mn75:23.11: His friends and companions, his relatives and kin, might bring him a surgeon to treat him.
mn75:23.12: The surgeon might make medicine for him—
mn75:23.13: an emetic, a purgative, an ointment, a counter-ointment, and treatment through the nose.
mn75:23.14: And through that medicine his eyesight might arise and be purified.
mn75:23.15: With the arising of his eyesight, whatever desire and lust he had for that grimy, oil-stained garment would be abandoned.
mn75:23.16: He might regard that man as an enemy, as a foe, and might even think he deserved to be put to death, saying:
mn75:23.17: ‘Indeed, sirs, for a long time I was tricked, deceived, and cheated by this man with this grimy, oil-stained garment—
mn75:23.18: “Good man, here is a white cloth for you, beautiful, spotless, and clean.”’
mn75:24.1: “So too, Māgaṇḍiya, were I to teach you the Dhamma thus:
mn75:24.3: you might come to know health, you might come to see Nibbāna.
mn75:24.4: With the arising of your eye, whatever desire and lust you had for the five aggregates affected by clinging would be abandoned;
mn75:24.5: and it might occur to you thus:
mn75:24.6: ‘Indeed, sirs, for a long time I was tricked, deceived, and cheated by this mind.
mn75:24.7: For clinging, I clung only to form; clinging, I clung only to feeling; clinging, I clung only to perception; clinging, I clung only to formations; clinging, I clung only to consciousness.
mn75:24.8: With my clinging as condition, being came to be; with being as condition, birth; with birth as condition, ageing and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair came to be;
mn75:24.9: such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering.’”
mn75:25.1: “I have such confidence in Master Gotama
mn75:25.2: that Master Gotama is able to teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might rise from this seat no longer blind.”
mn75:25.3: “In that case, Māgaṇḍiya, you should associate with true men.
mn75:25.4: When you associate with true men, Māgaṇḍiya, you will hear the true Dhamma;
mn75:25.5: when you hear the true Dhamma, you will practise in accordance with the Dhamma;
mn75:25.6: when you practise in accordance with the Dhamma, you will know for yourself and see for yourself:
mn75:25.8: and here diseases, boils, darts cease without remainder.
mn75:25.9: With the cessation of my clinging, being ceases; with the cessation of being, birth ceases; with the cessation of birth, ageing and death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease;
mn75:25.10: such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.’”
mn75:26.1: When this was said, Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer said to the Blessed One:
mn75:26.3: As though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who was lost, or holding up a lamp in the darkness so that those with eyes could see forms—so too the Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama.
mn75:26.4: I go to Master Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Sangha of bhikkhus.
mn75:26.5: I would receive the Going-forth under Master Gotama, I would receive the Full Admission.”
mn75:27.1: “Māgaṇḍiya, one who formerly belonged to another sect and wishes for the Going-forth and the Full Admission in this Dhamma and Discipline lives on probation for four months. At the end of the four months, bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give him the Going-forth into homelessness and the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state.
mn75:27.2: But even here I have recognized a difference between individuals.”
mn75:27.3: “Venerable sir, if those who formerly belonged to another sect and wish for the Going-forth and the Full Admission in this Dhamma and Discipline live on probation for four months, and at the end of four months bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give them the Going-forth into homelessness and the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state, then I will live on probation for four years, and at the end of the four years let bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give me the Going-forth into homelessness and the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state.”
mn75:28.1: And Māgaṇḍiya the Wanderer received the Going-forth in the Blessed One’s presence, and he received the Full Admission.
mn75:28.2: Not long after his Full Admission, the venerable Māgaṇḍiya, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, before long entered upon and abided in that supreme goal of the life divine, for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge here and now.
mn75:28.3: He directly knew: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’
mn75:28.4: And the venerable Māgaṇḍiya became one of the Arahants.
